quotes.text: Because if you keep building dashboards as the end product, you're not funding visibility. You're funding delay

quotes.text: If you remember nothing else, remember this. Dashboard support exploration, but event systems support decision velocity.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Every notification should answer four things before it ships. What changed? Why now? Who owns it? And what happens next?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Notifications are products, not side effects. They need owners. They need maintenance. They need life cycle reviews.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: Dashboards support exploration, but high-value decisions need event-driven notifications that push context to an owner when a business condition changes.
A notification architecture uses Power BI as a sensor, AI for anomaly detection and summaries, Power Automate for orchestration, Dataverse for state and feedback loops to tune the rules.
Treat notifications as products with owners, life cycle reviews and cost monitoring, and watch Teams payload limits, throttling and metered AI credits as you scale.
hook: Most dashboards die quietly because they depend on someone remembering to open them at the right time. This episode shows BI leads, Power Platform architects and executives how to shift from static reporting to a proactive notification blueprint with Power BI, Power Automate, Dataverse and AI that pushes action when it matters.
